items.title: Ever buy more than you mean to when shopping online? This could be why
A Montrealer died in Istanbul. Authorities blame food poisoning but what we found suggests something else
items.summary_auto: A young Canadian woman travelled to Turkey after graduating from medical school. In her last days there, she fell ill and died within hours. Authorities there blame food poisoning, but a joint investigation by Enquête and the fifth estate revealed 12 similar deaths and a different poison at work.

items.title: Why some Americans are stockpiling for a 90-day power outage
items.summary_auto: The number of Americans stockpiling bottled water, non-perishable food and other emergency supplies has spiked over the past few weeks, a trend that has only accelerated in the wake of a series of high-profile tech outages.

items.title: Canadian investment dollars are one of the villains in Spain’s election fight over housing
items.summary_auto: Canadian investment firms, led by Toronto-based Brookfield, have become central targets in Spain’s Nov. 29 election fight over housing affordability. Long-term Madrid tenants living in former public housing allege Brookfield plans to let their rent-controlled leases expire and sell their apartments at unaffordable market prices.

items.title: Large AI companies 'desperate for compute' are crowding out Canadian startups at home
items.summary_auto: Ottawa's new budget promises to help Canadian AI companies access AI processing power on home soil — something that's been a challenge as smaller startups face fierce competition from larger AI companies that are "desperate for compute."

items.title: Health-care report highlights chronic conditions, inequities in northern Ontario First Nations
items.summary_auto: A new report by an alliance of 11 First Nations health and social service agencies highlights health-care inequities facing northern Ontario communities, including high rates of rheumatoid arthritis, chronic pancreatitis and substance use disorder.

items.title: Orders roll in for Quebec company's quirky shipping boxes made from campaign posters
items.summary_auto: Quebec’s provincial election may be over, but the faces of the candidates are about to make a comeback.

items.title: How a small Toronto radio program is bringing Afghan women's voices to light
items.summary_auto: A Toronto radio program is providing the opportunity for women living under the Taliban regime to share their stories. Radio Jawan operates like a journalism school, and is run by a former reporter in Afghanistan who settled in the GTA

items.title: Sunrise on the Reaping may be a prequel, but it's the worst way to start The Hunger Games
items.summary_auto: The framing of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping as a painful, nihilistic and unrelentingly dour backstory for a single character makes it a deeply strange movie when viewed as a standalone feature.

items.title: Trump administration moves to drop lawsuit challenging Alaska Senate election result
items.summary_auto: The Trump administration on Thursday moved to effectively drop its lawsuit that sought to block the certification of Democrat Mary Peltola's victory in Alaska's U.S. Senate race, ending a much-criticized gambit by the president to prevent one of his political rivals from taking office.

items.title: Texas death row execution takes more than an hour as inmate heard complaining of pain
items.summary_auto: The execution of Reinaldo Dennes in Texas took over an hour as prison staffers struggled to find a suitable vein for the two intravenous needles carrying the lethal dose of the sedative pentobarbital. He was the second person put to death in the country Thursday after Florida carried out a record-breaking 20th execution of the year, of Thomas Mitchell Overton.

items.title: Sean Cairncross out, Kirsten A. Davies in as White House national cyber director: source
items.summary_auto: Sean Cairncross is out as the White House's national cyber director, a source close to the White House told CBC News on Thursday.

items.title: 'Crypto King' faked kidnapping, created video for sympathy, defence says
items.summary_auto: A lawyer defending one of so-called "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski’s alleged kidnappers says the kidnapping was a "farce" and that Pleterski created a video pretending to be kidnapped in order to gain sympathy from his investors, who were trying to recover funds from him.

items.title: CN derailments into Skeena River raise fresh concerns over shipping hazardous materials through northwest B.C.
items.summary_auto: The company says a suspected rockslide pushed a locomotive and several cars down an embankment and into the waters of the Skeena River Tuesday, with diesel from the locomotive then leaking more than a kilometre downstream. It's the second such incident this year, following a similar derailment during extreme weather this past March.

items.title: U.S. sanctions Italian mafia's alleged Canadian branch, including Toronto-area funeral homes
items.summary_auto: The United States on Thursday announced sanctions targeting what authorities described as the Canadian arm of the 'Ndrangheta, one of Italy's most powerful criminal organizations.

items.title: 9-month-old dies of hypothermia in Gaza as territory heads into winter season
items.summary_auto: Kinan Arqiq was nine months old when he died of hypothermia in Gaza, as heavy rains caused flooding in makeshift tent cities.

items.title: Former top Mountie, guilty of rec centre teen assault, gets conditional discharge
items.summary_auto: A former high-ranking B.C. RCMP officer has been granted a conditional discharge in an assault case stemming from an incident at the Abbotsford Recreation Centre in the summer of 2025.

items.title: Judge declares Meghan Markle's father fit to face charges related to child sexual abuse images
items.summary_auto: A U.S. judge in Florida ruled Thursday that Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, Britain's ‌Duchess of Sussex, is mentally competent to face a federal charge of possession of child pornography filed earlier this month.

items.title: Original Grand Theft Auto writer says GTA VI is ‘something close to a miracle’
items.summary_auto: When Brian Baglow was working on the first Grand Theft Auto in the mid-’90s, he had no idea it would spawn an iconic, decades long series, culminating in a blockbuster sixth installation that's shattering sales records and inspiring people to stay home from work.

items.title: This Sask. woman took some birds to a poultry show. Now avian flu is taking her whole flock
items.summary_auto: More than 18 million birds in Canada, including more than 1.2 million in Saskatchewan, have been lost due to the highly pathogenic disease since 2021.

items.title: Tumbler Ridge shooter used ChatGPT to build 3D gun parts, U.S. magazine reports
items.summary_auto: Mother Jones reports that ChatGPT helped killer Jesse Van Rootselaar make a 3D-printed gun magazine and foregrip, and gave advice on how to fix a spring, before the deadly mass shooting on Feb. 10.

items.title: Almost half of women in B.C. report intimate partner violence: StatsCan
items.summary_auto: The study showed 47 per cent of B.C. women reported experiencing intimate partner violence. That figure, calculated from 2025 data, has held steady since the last report, which examined numbers gathered in 2018.

items.title: Armed forces in Haiti push to oust gang members from corridor on edge of capital
items.summary_auto: Armed forces in Haiti launched an aggressive operation on Thursday to remove powerful gangs long entrenched in a key corridor that connects the country's capital to its western and southern regions.

items.title: Fiona the hippo dies after ingesting visitor's hat
items.summary_auto: The Cincinnati Zoo says Fiona the hippo, who became a social media darling after surviving her premature birth, has died, days after ingesting a visitor's hat.

items.title: Law firm has done $11.8M US worth of free legal work for Trump administration, Democrats say
items.summary_auto: U.S. congressional Democrats probing law firms that made deals with President Donald Trump's ‌administration said on Thursday that Kirkland & Ellis has provided at least $11.8 million US in free legal services to federal agencies.

items.title: Alleged co-conspirator in Tumbler Ridge shooting has trial delayed until December 2027
items.summary_auto: The trial for alleged Tumbler Ridge shooting co-conspirator Melody Bryant has been delayed from next month to December 2027 after she waived her right to a speedy trial and requested more time to review the discovery materials.

items.title: Leaked news release announces Konrad Narth will lead Manitoba PCs into election — before members vote
items.summary_auto: The Manitoba NDP obtained a leaked draft of a Progressive Conservative news release announcing Konrad Narth would lead the Tories into the 2027 election — before the party's executive council even voted on the possibility.

items.title: Petition asks Netflix to cancel The Body for 'blasphemous' and 'anti-Christian' content
items.summary_auto: The new Netflix show The Body is garnering backlash for being "blasphemous" and "anti-Christian," with over 110,000 people signing a petition asking Netflix to cancel the show. The Body, which released on the streaming platform on Nov. 11, is a coming-of-age drama by writer, actor and director Quinn Shephard that tells the story of a dance team at a Catholic school.

items.title: Reaching interim U.S. trade agreement would kickstart new CUSMA talks, minister says
Ubisoft cuts 166 jobs at Montreal and Quebec City video game studios
items.summary_auto: Ubisoft's head of public relations told Radio-Canada that the cuts impacted production teams as well as some workers who support production. The cuts aren't the first this year for Ubisoft's Canadian workforce — nor for the broader video game industry.

items.title: Ontario's former colleges and universities minister refuses to answer questions about growing OSAP scandal
items.summary_auto: Ontario's former minister of colleges and universities, who presided over the file for three years until 2024, is refusing to answer questions about a growing Ontario Student Assistance Program scandal.

items.title: Granby Zoo offers to rehome bat colony living in Quebec long-term care facility
items.summary_auto: Officials are still figuring out what do with the bats in a long-term care home in Sorel-Tracy, Que., where a rabies-infected bat came into contact with a resident earlier this month. One of the options being considered is transporting the colony to Granby Zoo's bat refuge.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is a love story. No to hiring sex workers, yes to buying your girlfriend flowers
items.summary_auto: Players jumping into Grand Theft Auto VI today may be surprised that they aren't able to commit some of the more morally objectionable acts that were possible in previous instalments.

items.title: Alberta government to revise policy as school boards say new flag regulations could cost millions of dollars
items.summary_auto: Alberta’s education and childcare minister says he will change an incoming school flags regulation that has school divisions collectively preparing to spend millions of dollars on hundreds of new outdoor flagpoles.

items.title: 'We could have been dead,' says tenant who escaped Cape Breton building collapse
items.summary_auto: Viola Baker says she was in bed Wednesday morning when she heard a big bang, and all of a sudden the walls started caving in. She rushed to help rescue her daughter and 15-year-old grandson.

items.title: 6 Canadian cities announced as stops on PWHL Takeover Tour
items.summary_auto: Edmonton, Calgary, Halifax, Saskatoon, Winnipeg and Quebec City will host games this upcoming season as part of the PWHL's Takeover Tour. The 24-game tour is the league's largest yet and will visit cities without PWHL teams.

items.title: Anthropic stock soars by double-digits, a 'big near-term win' for a 'very nervous' tech sector
items.summary_auto: Shares of Anthropic rose on their first day of trading, as investors weighted AI enthusiasm against a massive valuation and uncertain path to profitability.

items.title: Alberta bill would ban some bike lanes, let transportation minister remove others
items.summary_auto: Alberta’s government is proposing to ban future bike lanes that remove or restrict motor-vehicle traffic and give itself the power to remove some existing bike lanes.

items.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya ethnic minority, International Court of Justice rules
Ontario Northlander rail service to resume on Dec. 10
items.summary_auto: The Ontario Northlander passenger rail service is expected to return on Dec. 10, according to Ontario Northland.

items.title: Mother in Burlington, Ont., house fire over the weekend has died, family friend says
items.summary_auto: Talika 'Tilly' Stuart was one of five people rescued from a house fire on Saturday. Her husband and two of her children, 12 and 1, died as a result of their injuries. A five-year-old child was also injured.

items.title: Montreal byelections crucial for rebuilding NDP, party leader Avi Lewis says
items.summary_auto: Avi Lewis said a win in either Montreal byelection would be "incredible" but he sees these contests — and the four others taking place across Canada on Dec. 7 — as a means to continue building up the NDP's support base for the next general election.

items.title: Toys 'R' Us partnership has Staples Canada playing around with its business model
items.summary_auto: In a bid to bring back the beloved brand, Toys "R" Us and Parties "R" Us departments are moving into portions of 300 Staples Canada stores by the end of next year. Retail consultants say the office supply company is responding to the shrinking of the core business it's known for.

items.title: Water levels ‘critically low’ at Moose Factory Island water treatment plant in northern Ontario
items.summary_auto: Water levels at the water treatment plant on Moose Factory Island, in Ontario’s far north, are critically low, according to the Ontario Clean Water Agency.

items.title: KPMG Canada client documents accessed in cybersecurity breach, accounting firm says
items.summary_auto: KPMG did not provide details about the breach, including the scope or nature of the attack. But a spokesperson says the company is confident that the accessed data is not available online, or being misused for any purpose.

items.title: Watch this eagle be released into the wild, weeks after it was hit by a car
items.summary_auto: A bald eagle is back in the skies over Yukon, thanks to a chance encounter and a little help along the way. CBC's George Maratos has the story.

items.title: Dozens missing off Senegal as West African departures for Europe surge
items.summary_auto: Dozens of people were missing on Thursday after a boat carrying migrants bound for Europe capsized off the coast of Senegal, a local non-governmental organization said, in the latest incident along the West Africa route.

items.title: Fossil fuel limits cut from latest draft of UN climate deal
items.summary_auto: Climate negotiators stripped out any reference to ending the use of fossil fuels in a slimmed-down draft deal text published on Thursday, as ‌the COP31 meeting in Antalya, Turkey, approaches its Friday deadline.

items.title: Ella Langley sweeps Country Music Awards as Taylor Swift returns for 1st performance in 13 years
items.summary_auto: Ella Langley and her unstoppable hit Choosin' Texas dominated the Country Music Association Awards on Wednesday at ‌a ceremony that also featured Taylor Swift's first performance at the CMAs in 13 years.

items.title: Calgary’s condo market is shifting as supply outpaces demand
items.summary_auto: After years of increases, some sellers are now cutting asking prices by tens of thousands of dollars to attract buyers. And with more housing on the way, the pressure on prices may not be over.

Should playing O Canada be mandatory in all P.E.I. schools? One MLA thinks so
items.summary_auto: For decades, students in Canadian schools have started their day hearing the national anthem. Now, PC MLA Tyler DesRoches wants to make that mandatory across Prince Edward Island.

items.title: South Korea's top court overturns charges against ex-prime minister for his role in martial law
items.summary_auto: South Korea's Supreme Court on Thursday overturned the conviction of former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo for aiding in the declaration of martial law in December 2024.
